findings.rule: Tolerances tighter than a normal machining process can hold
findings.reasoning: Dimension D1 specifies 15 ±0.003 mm (6 µm total tolerance band). This is far tighter than standard milling, turning, or even routine grinding can reliably and economically hold on mild steel, making the part unnecessarily costly or impossible to produce as drawn.
findings.correction: Relax the tolerance on D1 to match the actual functional requirement; if a precision fit is needed, specify an appropriate ISO fit class (e.g., H7/g6) rather than an arbitrary ±0.003 mm limit.

findings.rule: Conflicting tolerances on the same feature
findings.reasoning: Feature F1 has two dimensions for the same 15 mm width: D1 calls it out as 15 ±0.003 mm while D4 calls it out as 15 with no explicit tolerance. These are contradictory specifications that will confuse manufacturing and inspection about which tolerance governs.
findings.correction: Remove the duplicate dimension or clearly indicate which one is reference (REF), ensuring only one governing tolerance applies to the 15 mm width of F1.

findings.rule: Conflict between general note and explicit dimension
findings.reasoning: Symbol S1 states 'UNSP.RADII 0.5 R', meaning all unspecified radii should be 0.5 mm. However, dimension D6 explicitly defines the radius of the semicircular slot (F5) as R 21.5 mm. If the drafter intended the slot root or edge to have a 0.5 mm radius, it conflicts with the explicit R 21.5 callout; if R 21.5 is the intended functional radius, the general note creates ambiguity.
findings.correction: Clarify whether the 0.5 R applies to the slot's fillet/edge by adding a specific radius callout at that location, or exclude the slot from the general note if R 21.5 is the sole intended radius.
